before.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

after.description: AS a Content Author, I WANT to preview draft entries in CMS, SO THAT I can see how content will be shown on the website. This requires adding live_preview configuration to the Contentstack SDK Stack initialization and threading preview query parameters (live_preview, live_preview_token, content_type_uid) through the existing data-fetching pipeline (getEntry, getSingleEntry, findSingletonEntry → ContentstackFactory) so that draft entries are fetched and rendered when preview mode is active. Limitation: Protected pages may not support preview.
after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
verificationCriteria: Given the Contentstack SDK client is mocked to return a draft entry when a live_preview_token is supplied, the rendered page displays the draft entry's title and body text instead of the published entry's title and body text

Given a request URL that includes live_preview=1 and live_preview_token=<token> and content_type_uid=<uid> query parameters, the Contentstack SDK query issued by getEntry or getSingleEntry or findSingletonEntry includes those preview parameters in its request to the Contentstack API

Given a request URL that does NOT include live_preview query parameters, the rendered page displays the same published content it displayed before this change, with no difference in layout, data, or behavior
Given the Contentstack Stack initialization options object, it contains a live_preview configuration property that enables the SDK's live preview capability

Given the Contentstack SDK client is mocked to return a draft entry, and the application receives preview parameters via the request URL, the page re-renders with the draft content without requiring a full page reload

Given a protected or authenticated page route, when preview parameters are present in the request URL, the page renders its current published content unchanged (acknowledged limitation — preview is not supported on protected pages)

notes: Novel capability — no live_preview config exists anywhere in the codebase (grep returned zero matches). The Contentstack SDK Stack initialization in src/services/contentstack.ts has no live_preview property, and none of the query-building methods accept preview tokens or content_type UIDs for draft fetching. The attachment point is the options object passed to contentstack.Stack() and the ContentstackFactory methods that construct all queries. The vendor documentation confirms that for App Router CSR, the SDK init needs a live_preview config object and individual queries must receive preview parameters (content_type_uid, live_preview_token) from the request context — this is application code, not just dashboard configuration. The 8-point estimate likely includes: (1) SDK config change, (2) threading preview params through getEntry/getSingleEntry/findSingletonEntry, (3) extracting preview params from the request URL on the client side, and (4) client-side re-rendering when Contentstack pushes preview updates. Protected pages are out of scope per the story's own limitation note. No getServerSideProps/getStaticProps were found — the project appears to use App Router CSR, which aligns with the referenced documentation's target architecture.

notes: Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with detailed technical analysis. All 16 criteria above are new. I read src/services/contentstack.ts and src/interface/contentstack.ts to ground the criteria in the actual codebase: (1) The options object at line ~55 has no live_preview property — AC-1 and AC-7 address config presence/absence. (2) ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeQuery and createContentTypeEntryQuery build all queries — AC-3/4/5 ensure preview params reach these query builders. (3) The three public methods getEntry, getSingleEntry, findSingletonEntry are the API surface — each gets its own AC for completeness. (4) The IContentstackGetEntry/GetSingleEntry/GetSingletonEntry interfaces lack preview fields — AC-13 covers the interface extension. (5) There is a separate interactive-maps Stack — AC-14 ensures it is not impacted. (6) The existing error handling uses try/catch with logger.error and re-throw — AC-8 follows the same pattern. (7) Cache policies exist via setCachePolicy — AC-10 prevents draft caching. (8) The management_token is a secret that must not leak — AC-11 addresses security. (9) The story explicitly notes protected pages as a limitation — AC-12 ensures preview doesn't bypass auth. (10) Contentstack live preview requires client-side re-rendering on push — AC-15 covers this. (11) AC-9 handles the edge case of partial preview params. (12) AC-16 handles the missing-management-token startup scenario, consistent with the existing pattern of startup validation in the file.
